title: Partial pooling and shrinkage
dek: Complete pooling: one θ. No pooling: a θⱼ per unit. Partial pooling: θⱼ share a distribution, so small units borrow strength. The weights are information, not taste.
story: Three estimators of district FQ-R. Complete pooling: π̂ = y_total / n_total. No pooling: π̂ⱼ = yⱼ/nⱼ. Partial pooling: π̂ⱼ is a weighted average of π̂ⱼ^{local} and a shared mean. When nⱼ = 4, the weight on the local fraction should be small. When nⱼ = 400, it should be large.

The Gaussian–Gaussian formula is the picture: E[θⱼ | y] = λⱼ ȳⱼ + (1−λⱼ) μ with λⱼ = τ² / (τ² + σ²/nⱼ). τ² is between-unit variance. If districts are nearly identical, τ² is small and everyone shrinks. If they are wildly different, τ² is large and you almost no-pool.

Exchangeability is the scientific licence: given the covariates you already put in the mean, you are willing to treat the leftover unit effects as draws from one distribution. A referral hospital is often not exchangeable with a rural clinic. Put “referral” in the mean; do not ask τ² to launder it.
deepTitle: Weights, hyperparameters, and bias on purpose
deep: λⱼ is Fisher-information geometry: local precision nⱼ/σ² versus prior precision 1/τ². Empirical Bayes plugs in τ̂, μ̂. Fully Bayes puts a posterior on τ and so a posterior on each λⱼ. When J (number of units) is small, τ̂ is noisy and shrinkage is uncertain — show that.

MSE: shrinkage is biased for each θⱼ toward μ and often wins on MSE for the small j. It can lose for a true outlier unit. That is why you inspect residuals at the unit level and consider a mixture of types, not one Normal.

Complete pooling is partial pooling with τ² = 0. No pooling is τ² = ∞. LRT of τ = 0 is a boundary test (hierarchical plate). AIC on a no-pooling dummy model uses a dishonest n if you then interpret dummies as a population.

In mutation catalogues, partial pooling across drugs in a class, or across genes in a pathway, is the same weights with a different index j. Do not pool across mechanisms you would never call exchangeable in lab meeting.

formulas.label: Gaussian–Gaussian weight
formulas.note: Weight on the local mean. Small nⱼ ⇒ small λⱼ ⇒ shrink toward μ.

visual.caption: Schematic estimates of four district rates. No pooling jumps around at small n. Complete pooling is a flat line. Partial pooling moves the small districts toward the shared mean and leaves the large one almost where it was.

example.title: 0/4 is not a different species from 12/50
example.setup: Districts: 0/4, 1/5, 3/40, 12/50. Survey mean about 16/99 ≈ 0.16. Normal approximation is crude for 0/4; the λ geometry still teaches.

steps.title: No pooling
steps.body: 0%, 20%, 7.5%, 24%. The map is a noise map.

steps.title: Guess τ
steps.body: If between-district SD on a probability scale is modest, λ for n=4 is small. 0/4 shrinks toward 16%, not to a published 0%. 12/50 barely moves.

steps.title: Better likelihood
steps.body: Use logit-normal or Beta-Binomial hierarchical, not a Normal on raw proportions. The moral of λⱼ survives; the Gaussian formula was a lantern, not the analysis.

example.takeaway: Shrinkage is weighted averaging with weights from nⱼ and τ². Publishing 0/4 as 0% refuses the weights.

check.prompt: In the Gaussian–Gaussian formula, increasing nⱼ:
choices: Increases λⱼ, less shrinkage toward μ
check.answer: Increases λⱼ, less shrinkage toward μ
check.why: λ = τ² / (τ² + σ²/n). Bigger n shrinks the second term, λ → 1.

whyWrong.Sets τ² to 0: τ² is a hyperparameter, not a function of one nⱼ.

check.why: σ²/n = 1, λ = 1/(1+1) = 0.5. Equal weight on local mean and μ.

whyWrong.0.2: If you used n not σ²/n.

check.prompt: On the small-multiples, the n=4 district’s partial-pool bar sits between no-pool and complete-pool because:
check.figureHint: Left panel: no pool ~0, partial mid, pool ~survey mean.
choices: Partial pooling is a coin flip independent of n
Small-n units are pulled toward the shared mean but not all the way unless τ² = 0
Complete pooling uses only that district
No pooling is a Bayes estimator
check.answer: Small-n units are pulled toward the shared mean but not all the way unless τ² = 0
check.why: That interpolation is the definition of partial pooling.

whyWrong.No pooling is a Bayes estimator: No pooling ignores the shared prior.
